dlg.ui.leave: That will be all for now.
dlg.ui.present.title: Put a piece of evidence in front of them:
dlg.ui.present.none: The casebook is empty -- there is nothing to show yet.
dlg.colette.root.1: Good morning to you, detective -- or what the storm left of it. Colette Beaumont; I keep the kitchen and the books of this house.
dlg.colette.root.2: Thirty-one years I have baked in that kitchen, and no morning began worse than this one. Ask me what you like; I hide nothing worth hiding.
dlg.colette.root.c2: Who came and went by the doors?
dlg.colette.root.c3: Tell me about the garden door.
dlg.colette.evening.1: Supper at half six, and he ate alone in the parlour -- the gout, you understand. I served, I cleared, and I left him to his papers.
dlg.colette.evening.2: At half past ten I started the morning's bread and shut the kitchen door. The wireless on, the ovens warm -- my little world in order.
dlg.colette.evening.3: Then the dark came down at twenty to eleven like a lid. I lit the pantry lantern and baked through it. Where there is work, there is no fear -- that is my philosophy.
dlg.colette.comings.1: By the front door? One visitor only -- Mr. Ashcombe, the agent, at nine o'clock. Gone by a quarter past ten; it is written in my ledger in my own hand.
dlg.colette.comings.2: No one else came to that door all night, I would swear it on the bread. The rest of the coming and going was household, and in the dark a house is all elbows.
dlg.colette.garden.1: I found it at half eleven, fetching the milk in -- off its bolt, and the scratches on the latch plate bright as new pennies.
dlg.colette.garden.2: I bolted it and thought: did I leave it so? I did not, detective. Thirty-one years, and I have never once left it so.
dlg.colette.garden.3: Someone used that door while the house sat dark. It was not me -- I had my hands full of flour and my back to that wall all night.
dlg.colette.dark.1: The wireless died mid-song -- a singer I did not like, though I missed her all the same. The house went black as a pocket.
dlg.colette.dark.2: The loaf burnt, mind -- my one casualty of the storm. The birds forgave me before the lights were back.
dlg.colette.dark.3: At five past seven I took up the tea tray and found him. I dropped the tray. Peggy came running. The rest you know.
dlg.colette.present_miss.1: I couldn't speak to that, detective. The kitchen keeps me busy, and the kitchen keeps me honest.
dlg.colette.present_again.1: You have shown me that already, detective. My answer has not improved with age.
dlg.colette.bye.1: There is tea in the pot when the questions run dry, detective. In this house there is always tea.
dlg.colette.r_ledger.1: My own hand, that. 'Mr. A. at nine, gone quarter past ten.' The front door kept better order than the parlour did, if the truth is told.
dlg.colette.r_coats.1: No doctor's coat, no second umbrella, and that empty peg holds nothing but the house's own dust. If the doctor came, detective, she did not come by my hall.
dlg.colette.r_button.1: That is Tobias's horn button. Off his coat since Tuesday, he told me at breakfast -- the stair carpet swallows them and gives them back weeks later.
dlg.colette.r_gbolt.1: You have seen the scratches yourself, then. Bright and fresh and wrong. Whoever made them had no key to that door's habits -- only a reason.
dlg.colette.r_scissors.1: Miss Peggy's sewing scissors. She was down for them at twenty to eleven -- I heard her on the stair, and him humming like a boy. Humming, detective, at twenty to eleven.
dlg.colette.r_glass.1: I never touch the whiskey tray, detective. That was the master's own nightly ritual, drops and all, and I respected it the way one respects a clock.
dlg.colette.r_decanter.1: The decanter lived at his elbow, detective, not in the cabinet. If something got into it, it got in after supper -- and there were six of us, then five, then... I miscount. Forgive me. There were visitors and hours and dark.
dlg.colette.r_ash.1: I rake that hearth every morning, and this morning it had a smell I did not know -- sweet, like hay and honey. Not a cooking smell. I did not like it.
dlg.colette.r_clock.1: I dust it, I never wind it -- that was his nightly ceremony, winding the clock before bed. He loved that clock like family. Better than some family, if you follow me.
dlg.colette.r_pills.1: His drops at seven o'clock sharp, five in water, doctor's orders. I set out the glass and the bottle myself, every evening, and every morning the bottle was just as the doctor left it.
dlg.colette.r_memoir.1: He talked of 'putting things right' on Monday, he did -- like a man settling accounts before a journey. I minded my bread and let him mind his pages.
dlg.colette.r_body.1: I found him so, detective, except my tray was in one piece and my breath was not. He looked like a man asleep in the middle of a good page. Except that he was cold.
dlg.tobias.root.1: Oh -- good morning, sir. Tobias Grimm. Apprentice. I'm sorry about the ink -- I came down as soon as Colette cried out, and it does not wash out before... well. Before this.
dlg.tobias.root.2: Ask me anything, sir. I have been going over the night in my head all morning, line by line, like a page I botched.
dlg.tobias.root.c2: What did you hear in the night?
dlg.tobias.attic.1: Inking Chapter Six, sir -- the Whistler book is due Monday and the master wanted the cross-hatching 'breathing' by Sunday. So: half seven in the attic, pencil down at midnight.
dlg.tobias.attic.2: The storm killed the lights at twenty to eleven -- my line stops mid-stroke, you will see it on the board. I sat in the dark a while, then finished the panel by candle.
dlg.tobias.attic.3: When the lamps came back the house felt... held, sir. Like a breath being kept. I do not know how else to say it.
dlg.tobias.heard.1: Thunder, mostly. The rain working the windows. And then -- sir, I told the Sergeant this -- a clatter, like a clock falling, a few minutes after half eleven.
dlg.tobias.heard.2: Then quiet. The quiet I mind more than the clatter, sir. An old house is never truly quiet, and it was truly quiet after that.
dlg.tobias.clockfell.1: That was the mantel clock, then -- the one on the parlour mantel, his father's. I heard it fall from two floors up and through a closed door, sir. That is a heavy clock.
dlg.tobias.clockfell.2: He must have been reaching for something when it went. The bell-pull, maybe. And then the quiet.
dlg.tobias.master.1: He took me on at twenty-three, off a portfolio of clock faces -- no one else looked twice at it. He taught me the hand before the eye, sir: 'the line must mean it, not just say it.'
dlg.tobias.master.2: My inking is my own, sir. The stories were always his. I would ink his pages till my eyes gave out and be glad of it.
dlg.tobias.present_miss.1: I could not speak to that, sir. I keep to my desk, and my desk keeps to the attic.
dlg.tobias.present_again.1: I have seen that one already, sir. It did not grow clearer for the second look.
dlg.tobias.bye.1: I will be at my board, sir. Chapter Six waits for no inquest.
dlg.tobias.r_mantel.1: Face-in at 11:38. Then my clatter and the fallen clock are one and the same, sir -- put my ears down for eleven thirty-eight and some minutes. 'After half eleven' was all I would swear before; now I can say it better.
dlg.tobias.r_button.1: That is mine, sir -- off my coat since Tuesday, there are spares in my sewing tin, ask Colette. The stair carpet has been eating my buttons since I was nineteen.
dlg.tobias.r_clock.1: Two floors up I heard it stop... no, that is foolishness, sir, you cannot hear a clock stop. I saw it stopped, coming down this morning. The whole house ran on that clock.
dlg.tobias.r_glass.1: I do not drink, sir. Ink is my poison and I take it professionally.
dlg.tobias.r_slip.1: Pages for 'H.M.', sir? I ink what I am handed -- numbered, quoted, signed for. The master kept his own correspondence, and I keep my pencil where it belongs.
dlg.tobias.r_memoir.1: He read me the preface on Thursday, sir, and it was fine -- but he did not read me the middle. He said the middle was 'for a friend first.'
dlg.tobias.r_decanter.1: The whiskey was his, sir, down to the ritual of it. I would not have known which shelf it lived on.
dlg.tobias.r_body.1: I looked in before the Sergeant came, sir, from the door only. I could not-- he looked like a page left half turned. I went back to the attic and sharpened pencils for an hour.
dlg.tobias.r_ash.1: I do not know flowers, sir, beyond what I have to draw. If there were petals in the fire, they were someone else's petals.
dlg.peggy.root.1: Detective. Margaret Vesper-Croft -- Peggy, to everyone who knew him. I am staying on until... until the house knows what it is.
dlg.peggy.root.2: I have answered the Sergeant's questions and I will answer yours. Only -- ask them kindly. He was my uncle, not my alibi.
dlg.peggy.root.c1: Your evening, in your own words.
dlg.peggy.evening.1: In my room from half past eight -- a novel and my sewing, the wireless down in the kitchen, the storm doing its worst upstairs and out.
dlg.peggy.evening.2: Asleep before eleven. I remember the hall clock being wound -- he always wound it before bed, poor darling, it was a whole ceremony. And then the thunder woke me once, and that was all.
dlg.peggy.uncle.1: My mother's brother, and the last of the family I had. Eight months ago I came to keep house for him -- the housekeeping and the worry of him, both.
dlg.peggy.uncle.2: His heart was poor, detective, but his spirits of late were high. He had a project -- he said it would 'put old matters right.' He was cheerful the way he had not been in years.
dlg.peggy.letter.1: You have been in the mail tray. Tuesday is family business, detective -- my uncle's will is his affair and mine, and no one's third.
dlg.peggy.letter.2: Ask me what I wore to dinner if you like. That letter I will not discuss.
dlg.peggy.scissors.1: They are mine -- you have found me out in sloppiness, at least. I came down at twenty to eleven; my sewing basket was short its scissors.
dlg.peggy.scissors.2: He was crossing the hall, detective. Humming. A folder of pages under his arm, and he ruffled my hair as if I were nine again, and told me to run along to bed.
dlg.peggy.scissors.3: I left the scissors on the sideboard like a fool and went back up. I sewed until the thunder, and I slept. That is my whole night, and every word of it true.
dlg.peggy.money.1: The lending office writes to me, detective, not to him. My debts are my own -- a bad year, bad company, the usual story.
dlg.peggy.money.2: He never knew the size of them. I would have sold every stick I own before I asked that man for money, and I never had to. Never.
dlg.peggy.present_miss.1: I do not know what you mean me to see in that, detective.
dlg.peggy.present_again.1: You have put that in front of me already. It has not changed, and neither have I.
dlg.peggy.bye.1: Close the door gently behind you, detective. He liked a door shut without a slam.
dlg.peggy.r_clock.1: Wound before bed? But it stopped with the storm at twenty to eleven -- you said so yourself -- and nobody wound it after. I heard it, you see. I heard...
dlg.peggy.r_clock.2: ...Then I dreamed the winding, detective. I half-woke at the thunder, and no more. Everything else I have told you is true. Everything.
dlg.peggy.r_scissors.1: Yes -- mine, and I will say it plainly since you have them in your book. I was down at twenty to eleven. He was alive and cheerful and humming, with a folder under his arm. Write that down: alive at twenty to eleven.
dlg.peggy.r_pills.1: His drops -- the doctor's label. He took them religiously at seven, five in water. Dr. Marsh kept his heart steady for years; he trusted her absolutely.
dlg.peggy.r_slip.1: 'H.M.' -- Dr. Marsh, surely. He trusted her absolutely, detective. Absolutely.
dlg.peggy.r_memoir.1: So that is the folder he carried -- 'A Confession of Sorts.' He said the book would put old matters right before Monday. He was humming, detective. Humming.
dlg.peggy.r_glass.1: His nightcap, regular as the clock. One glass, never two, and I brought up the tray some nights myself. Colette poured more often than I did.
dlg.peggy.r_ash.1: He liked a small fire even in October -- the hearth was lit from six. If someone burned flowers in it, they did it under his nose while the house sat dark.
dlg.peggy.r_body.1: Do not -- detective, do not make me look at him again today. I saw enough at seven o'clock to last me the rest of mine.
dlg.peggy.r_coats.1: My mac, Tobias's oilskin, uncle's raincoat -- and the fourth peg for callers. It has been empty a long while, I think.
dlg.peggy.r_button.1: Not mine -- my sewing loses pins, not buttons, detective.
dlg.peggy.r_ledger.1: Colette's ledger does not lie, detective. Whatever else in this house does.
dlg.captain.root.1: Byrne. Door was open, so either you wanted my desk or the rain wanted you. Sit.
dlg.captain.root.2: Whatever it is, say it plainly. I run this place on plain speaking and bad coffee.
dlg.captain.q.files: The folders on my desk -- which one is mine?
dlg.captain.q.advice_first: Any advice before I take my first case?
dlg.captain.files.1: The desk takes care of itself. Four folders and a grey box. Vesper is yours -- Hollow Lane, Saturday night, a philanthropist with five houseguests and poison in his glass.
dlg.captain.files.2: The pier drowning is Grade II and you are a week into Grade I. The buttonmaker ledger is still being typed. The grey box from 1931 stays in the evidence room until I say otherwise.
dlg.captain.files.3: One folder, Detective. Take it, read it twice, and go stand where it happened.
dlg.captain.precinct.1: Old Town keeps this precinct fed: pawnshops, trams, and weather. The building is older than the street and the boiler is older than the building.
dlg.captain.precinct.2: Hollis holds the floor together. Dewi runs errands. The typing pool types at the speed of gossip. And the evidence room takes a signed key -- mine, mostly mine.
dlg.captain.advice_first.1: Three things. Read everything. Write everything. And never ask a question you already know the answer to -- ask the one you don't.
dlg.captain.advice_first.2: Your first case will try to introduce itself as an accident. Accidents are rare; posture is common.
dlg.captain.advice_first.3: And Byrne -- being a detective is mostly being wrong in an orderly fashion until the facts get embarrassed and confess. Go on.
dlg.captain.advice_case.1: Hollow Lane is a full house and one of them lies well. So: write it all down, connect it twice before you accuse once, and keep your magnifier dry.
dlg.captain.advice_case.2: When you can put the what, the who and the why in one sentence that survives me reading it -- you can name your man.
dlg.captain.hollis.1: Hollis took your statement exam, drank your terrible coffee, and told me the boy reads rooms like shelves -- slowly, twice, out of order. That was a recommendation. Take it seriously.
dlg.hollis.root.1: Byrne! Still got that records-room squint, I see. Good -- keep it. It catches what people leave lying about.
dlg.hollis.q.hollow: What do you know about Hollow Lane?
dlg.hollis.q.before_case: I haven't taken a folder yet.
dlg.hollis.q.mentor: How long have you been pushing paper here?
dlg.hollis.hollow.1: Seven Hollow Lane. Old Vesper's place. Saturday night the storm came down the chimney like a debt collector, and by midnight he was face-down in his own parlour.
dlg.hollis.hollow.2: I took the morning statements from the five guests -- they're in your file, word for word, no polish. Read 'em against each other. Rooms talk, Byrne; people just do it slower.
dlg.hollis.before_case.1: Then don't stand there looking hungry. Your desk, front and center, folders on it. Breche left one for you -- the Vesper file.
dlg.hollis.before_case.2: First case is a badge on one side and a weight on the other. Take it before the rain does.
dlg.hollis.mentor.1: Long enough to remember the last fellow with desk 14. Promoted twice, vanished into the archive one afternoon. They found his kettle. They never found him.
dlg.hollis.mentor.3: Mostly. Listen -- you read every file on the night shift for three years. That's the whole trade in miniature: names, gaps, and the one drawer nobody shut properly.
dlg.hollis.weather.1: Rain since Friday. The gutters have opinions and the tram wires sing. Perfect weather for a lie to stay indoors.
